We have several of these chairs which we love to use when we go to the river or on camping trips. The chairs weigh less than two pounds in their carry sack and they just take a few minutes to set up and use. The chair's frame is made of lightweight aircraft aluminum that's shock corded together and practically snaps together on its own.

Just slip the sections together, secure the ends into the plastic housing, and then attach the ends to the slots in the chair. It's easier if you attach the bottom before the back. When assembled the bottom of the seat is approximately 14" from the ground, the seat is about 21" across, and the back is about 26" high.

While that may seem small, the chair is actually very comfortable for a full grown adult to sit in. The chair has a maximum weight tolerance of 220 pounds, and it feels nice and steady when you sit in it. It is low to the ground though, so people with arthritis, hip or knee problems, or other mobility issues might require assistance to sit or stand back up.

The chair disassembles as easily as it assembles, and it's easy to get it back into the carry bag when you're finished using it. This chair is really convenient to take along for outdoor sporting events, concerts, fishing, camping, and virtually any outdoor activity, and it doesn't take up much space to store either. Enjoy!
.

It was a "manual" kind - the interior had something like rock wool that was soaked in butane and lit and then the metal casing was slid inside a thick insulated bag and put in your pocket.  It could get rather hot!  I mention this because it brings back fond memories, but also to illustrate the difference in the "old fashioned" hand warmers and this one.  I love how easy this is to charge, even in my car, and the 3 levels of warmth depending on how cold it is and/or what you are doing.  I can put this in my pocket on low heat while I'm scraping the ice off my windshield and windows, then grab the warmer and let my fingers regain some feeling before trading the scraper for the shovel and shoveling the snow away from the car and off the sidewalk.  However many times I need to, I can stop shoveling and grab the warmer to keep my hands and fingers from going numb - that's what I appreciate having this handwarmer!  If you have kids that wait at the bus stop or have to walk to school even in winter, giving them a handwarmer might be just the thing to give them a "boost" of warmth while standing in the cold!

Emerging Green – Foldable Meditation Bench, Durable Bamboo Folding Bench for Meditation and Relaxation, Meditation Stool with a Cotton Carrying Bag, Beige, 2.8 lbs I have been trying to meditate more regularly for some time now. I often sit on cushions or blankets, and have never used a bench. For my body, this little meditation bench makes sitting SO much more comfortable! The wood is bamboo; it's super-smooth and feels quite sturdy. The little legs are on quality hinges. There is a slight angle to the bottom of the legs so that the seat of the bench is on a gentle slope, allowing for a comfortable angle to sit on with a straight spine. The width is just under 18", wide enough for my fairly generous bottom, yet both the seat of the bench and the space underneath (where your ankles/calves go) could feel constricting for some body types.

The bench is fairly heavy, so I think it's mainly for home use (as opposed to travel), but the folding legs make it easy to store out of the way. I will note that the hinges on the legs don't snap into place, so they flop around if you are moving the bench. Overall, this a comfortable, quality, and convenient bench for meditation, and I definitely recommend it for body types/sizes similar to my own (see photo). However, note that those with larger bodies might not find this bench nearly as comfortable as I did.

text_fidelity_a:
Green Guru Gear Dutchy Bike Bicycle Bike Upcycled Made in USA Pannier Bag (design may vary) I did not purchase these on Amazon, but direct from the sellers (Green Guru Gear) website. I got an EBike (Aventon Pace 500) for commuting to work and needed something to hold my personal items for a post-ride, pre-work shower. These pannier bags fill the need excellently. You can hold a lot of items in there. Everything I can fit in my gym bag, which is pretty big, I can fit in these two panniers. In addition, I can fit my full lunch bag as well. My feet do not hit the bags when I peddle. If I choose to, I could also fit my purse/backpack in them, but I carry that on my back just for more security when I ride.

I had a Topeak MTX Quick track rear rack installed on my bike to use the MTX basket with and these panniers fit perfectly on them. I can actually use the panniers and the basket at the same time because the hooks on the panniers are flush with the top of the bags and the tops of the bags are level with the top of the rack itself, so the basket can slide onto the Quick track easily with the panniers in place. So if you have even more stuff to haul on the bicycle you have all that extra space with the basket as well. Double check the weight limits on the bags and the rack before you do that though.

I knew the print on the panniers would be randomly selected when I placed my order, but I did note that they mentioned that they will try and match them if you purchase a pair, they did pretty good as both of them were in nice brown tones with pretty cool pictures/patterns on them. The bags are pretty simple to install on the rack, just hook them on and I wrap the bottom securing hook around the rack supports and hook it on sideways. The bags do not come out or off even if I go over big bumps in the road. As far as I can see about its "waterproof-ness" the material used on the cover and the front bottom half of the bags look more water "resistant", if its a few sprinkles or a light rain, it would hold up, but not a continuous downpour, especially since the sides of the bag don't appear to be water proof/resistant. The cover is secured to the front of the bag by hook & loop (Velcro) patches, they are pretty strong but cannot be locked, so if you require extra security get some type of cover to go over or secure it even more with bungee cords/nets. If you are so inclined, you could even sew on some straps with securing clips on them.

If I don't use the basket with the bags, they are easy to remove and carry. Carry by the short handles or the adjustable and convenient shoulder straps as well. They fold up for easy, low profile storage when not in use, either on the bike rack or somewhere else. I would not leave these unattended on a bicycle, they are so nice that someone may be tempted to steal them (probably those same crumbs that take the bicycle lights if you don't take them with you). If I use the basket also, it will have to be removed before removing the bags.

Overall, I am happy with my purchase of the Green Guru Dutchy pannier bags, I would recommend them for anyone considering getting panniers for your bicycle rack(s). They are great looking on the bicycle and pretty unique from other panniers.
text_fidelity_b: Green Guru Gear Dutchy Bike Bicycle Bike Upcycled Made in USA Pannier Bag (design may vary)

I took my time because some reviews cited the mount as a weak link as well as disputing whether or not this is the 'brightest'. I will admit that the mount seems flimsy, but in six weeks of relatively hard use it has held up.

As for brightness, I cannot say that it is or isn't the brightest. I will say that it illuminates a narrow path in front of you and definitely is oncoming driver friendly.

One thing about the mount is it will snap the light in place and firmly hold it if you follow the instruction sheet. It also quick releases the light so it will not get stolen when you chain your bike and go shopping or whatever. Plus it, like the tail light, installs without tools. I love that feature. I also love the fact that this light charges using a standard USB cable and not some proprietary one with a barrel connector. That is one of the reasons why I awarded this five stars.

Since the product specs cover the use and charging times in depth, I will not recite them here. I will say that I run mine at 100% brightness all the time and the 1.5 hour use time is fairly accurate.

There may be better lights on the market, but not at this one's price. I am thoroughly pleased with it and happy that I gave it six weeks before rushing to review it. In my opinion there is nothing seriously wrong with it and a lot that is right.

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports NCAA Team Licensed College Football Backpack - Official Logos and Colors - Heather Gray - 18" x 12" x 4" When I saw this Gator backpack by Franklin I was excited to get it - but now that I’ve used it I am left underwhelmed.

The logo is EXCELLENT. The modern Albert head logo embroidered on a royal blue field circled in orange - affixed permanently to the heather grey shell outer fabric of the backpack does look great.

Unfortunately that is about the extent of what I like about this backpack.

The outer shell material is excessively stiff and the inner liner shell feels like cheap polyvinyl material that crinkles loudly anytime you move it.

The overall design makes poor use of space and offers almost no built in organization methods, unlike most backpacks.

The outer pocket, where typical backpacks have an area to hold things you need to access easily - writing utensils, keys, wallet, etc - this one opens to a large pocket that encompasses the entire front with only a small mesh divider that rises to the level of the zipper. If you attempt to keep something there the first time the backpack is carried in any way but vertical everything in this pouch mixes within the larger front pocket.

Each side has mesh places to hold water bottles or possibly an umbrella. Unfortunately these are made so small that while you can force a typical water bottle into it - it’s not easy.

The main compartment has 1 divided area that is created with the crinkly material and elastic. It will hold a small laptop but the depth of this bag is so minimal that if that was in it there would be little room for anything else.

While the ergonomically shaped straps have padding and meshed fabric for ventilation the back does not.

The bottom of the bag has 2 zippers that open and reveal the ball hammock that extends from one pocket then buckle clips within the other with 2 plastic buckles. I managed to use this to hold a beach towel once but for the most part I’ve found that feature a waste.

At this price point there are vastly superior backpack options. In regards to functionality, overall design and materials used this backpack is poor and I would not recommend it.

I would advise finding another Gator backpack or attaching an embroidered Gator logo to a quality backpack.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports NCAA Team Licensed College Football Backpack - Official Logos and Colors - Heather Gray - 18" x 12" x 4"

text_fidelity_a:
Spyderco Tighe Stick Plain Edge Folding Knife with 3.90" Blade When I first opened the soft case that this knife came in my initial response was "WOW". What a beautiful looking piece of art! Brian Tighe is a highly respected knife innovator with 30 years of experience and valuable tactical expertise. He specializes in making top-quality custom tactical knives that start in the mid-$500's and go up into the thousands of dollars. If you call up his website you will see why he is so highly regarded.

This is Mr. Tighe's first collaboration with Spyderco and he has hit a home run. Unfortunately some of Spyderco's collaborations with famous knife makers come in as a disappointment, not as dramatic as the maker is capable of, somewhat dull and often under-built. Not this Tighe Stick however. It is a real beauty. The picture on the Amazon product page doesn't do it justice. The solid titanium scales give a real 3D appearance to the handle that is perfectly accented by the beautifully cut and sharp blade. This knife fits my (somewhat) large hand as though built for it and inspires instant confidence in the holder. I am not a knife fighter but the tactical aspects of this knife practically scream "look out".

And look out you should when handling the blade. It conquers the paper test like it's not even there. The tip of the blade is obviously sharp enough to pierce just about any material and there is absolutely no blade slop (wobble) when the blade is extended. I like carrying large knives to know that I can handle just about any project it is subjected to. On the other hand, this thing is so darn beautiful that it might end up in a display case with some of my other curved blades. If you want to own an excellent example of a Spyderco collaboration, this is your knife.

I was fortunate to pick this up 'on sale' at a specialty knife seller and had to post this review to let prospective customers know what a great build and value this knife is. Now if I can only find a Spyderco Brend-PireIa Mamba on sale I will be one happy collector.
text_fidelity_b: Spyderco Tighe Stick Plain Edge Folding Knife with 3.90" Blade

text_fidelity_a:
Withings Pulse While I am only ten days into using my Withings Pulse Ox, I am very pleased with the purchase so far. Of all the devices currently on the market, this one seemed to offer the most bang for the buck. The step, activity, and sleep tracking seem to be quite accurate. The pulse and oxygen saturation monitoring are simple and precise. Battery life seems to be superb, and integration/connectivity with my iPhone have been no problem. Both the wristband and the belt clip are well-made and comfortable. I find that it really helps to motivate me to maintain and improve my health.

If I were to provide four pieces of constructive criticism they would be:
1) Make the Pulse OX waterproof or at least very water resistant.
2) Improve the Apple Healthkit Integration. I've had some issues, not in the Withings App, but within Healthkit, with doubling of steps.
3) Provide a means for background measurement of pulse and oxygen, rather than requiring the fingertip read. It is not practical to use for Zone Training or to see peak heart rate during a workout.
4) Allow for customization of the step and sleep goals.

Overall it has been a great little device though. Used in my "App Ecosystem" of the Withings App, WebMD, MapMyRun, and Healthkit...it is a nearly complete solution for my personal wellness goals.
text_fidelity_b: Withings Pulse

Prevention Easy Healing Stretches: Follow-Along Routines - Guided Stretching routines to Alleviate Pain, Boost Energy, and Feel Amazing Kathi Ross-Nash is a wise, beautiful and elegant instructor who obviously has a lot of experience with Pilates and yoga. She has a slim, toned and strong body and can do exercises with advanced precision. It is a joy to watch her body move through all the poses and stretches and I especially loved how her makeup was done. Her voice and chatty style lulled me into a relaxed state almost like hypnosis. I found her instructions calming and soothing.

Some of the exercises are done in a chair like the face and neck exercises. You will do shoulder shrugs and stretch the neck side to side. Then you will do eye exercises and facial exercises that help relax your jaw. You may find these exercises and stretches especially healing if you work on a computer all day or if you tend to clench your jaw from stress.

Other exercises are done on the floor with a yoga mat. The hip exercises and stretches have some easy and advanced poses that are inspired by Pilates. The leg stretches can be modified with yoga blocks and include active stretching that test endurance and strength. You will move quickly from one pose to another.

For the Feet and Calves you will need a chair and two yoga blocks. If you've never exercised your feet before like this you may want to take the rest of the day off or try the chest openers next.

The Chest stretching was actually one of my favorite parts of this DVD. You will feel your core being strengthened too. You will need a strap - a yoga one works great.

To do some of these stretches you will need to be able to get down onto the floor and back up again. Not so easy for me now that I'm over 50 but I pushed through and did it anyways. So I would say this DVD also tests your resilience and endurance not to mention patience and flexibility. I could have easily done all these exercises with no problem in my 20s, 30s and 40s! So if you do a lot of yoga and Pilates you may find these exercises very relaxing and invigorating.

There is a bar on the left side of the screen to clue you in to how long you still have until completion of each section. It is not distracting once you get used to it and seems helpful.

Some of the props you will need include 2 yoga blocks, a strap, a clean dry washcloth, a rubber band and a small ball for the foot exercises. I managed without the small ball but definitely used the strap and found a rubber band in my drawer that worked. The washcloth is used for the jaw stretches but nowhere else.

Some of my other favorite DVDs for Stretching and Strengthening include:

Simply Stretch by Jessica Smith
Yoga for Inflexible People
Pilates on the Go by Maria Leone
Face Aerobics
Karen Voight Full Body Stretch
Stretch and Strength by Anne Pringle Burnell (Especially geared for those over 50!)

I think it is a worthy goal to collect as many of these excellent DVDs as you can because stretching DVDs are what you need to feel good and flexible as you age. This Easy Healing Stretches DVD has five sections that you can do over a period of days to increase your whole body's strength and tone. Enjoy!

~The Rebecca Review
text_fidelity_b: Prevention Easy Healing Stretches: Follow-Along Routines - Guided Stretching routines to Alleviate Pain, Boost Energy, and Feel Amazing

I needed it for a high-heat application, the cord had to resist temperatures of about 400F and retain its strength. This will certainly do that.

Some notes, though - this is Kevlar, so it frays at the ends. To seal it, you'll want to use an epoxy or the equivalent, you cannot melt the strands together, they just glow or turn to ash. This cord is fairly abrasive compared to many other synthetics, so if it is going to be in rubbing up against other materials (or skin) damage may result. It also doesn't seem to hold knots quite as well as I'm used to, but that may be technique.

Anyway, it worked for my purposes, so if you specifically need the characteristics of Kevlar, this is a good way to go, the quality of the product seems to be quite good. Otherwise, I'd go with a different material.

1 Star: I never got what I expected from the product. Would not buy the product again, requested a refund or returned the product. (This is very rare for me.) I do not recommend buying this product whatsoever.

Previously I was using a small rechargeable light that was more for visibility to oncoming cars than to actually see the ground.

This extra illumination of this light has made a significant difference for me when commuting at night. I used to avoid areas with low illumination. The XOSS illuminates the ground in front like a car headlight allowing me to ride in total darkness. I tilt the light so can see everything coming at me from about 20-30 feet away, which is enough time to react at my normal riding speed.

I have also used both the automatic on/off motion sensor and standard on/off modes and they each worked well.

The handlebar attachment/removal system allows me to use the XOSS as a flashlight (have done this several times) and more easily charge it. However, the attachment clip has an issue - if you tighten it onto the handlebars too much, the screw will enter a hole on the bottom of the light and restrict it from being put on or removed. Be aware...

Recommended!

(update) The bracket snapped under fairly normal usage. Maybe it was the cold weather making the plastic a bit brittle... Rather than toss the light or turn it into a flashlight, I 3D printed a replacement part. You can find it on thingiverse. Just search for "XOSS Enfitnix Bike Headlight Bracket"

text_fidelity_a:
Klymit Inertia O Zone Lightweight Camping Air Pad If you’re looking for a camping mat to accompany you on long hikes and week-long camping trips in the middle of nowhere, look no further. This mat weighs in at just 12.2 oz., which makes it one of the most lightweight options out there for individuals looking to go ultra-light. In addition to adding hardly any weight to your pack, this sleeping mat is also compact. The packaging this comes in claims the size is comparable to a soda can of some sort, which is only slightly accurate. Needless to say, it’s bigger than a soda can, but really only by an inch or two either way. It’s still incredibly tiny compared to every other sleeping pack I have carried.

The diagram suggests you can blow this particular mat up in 5 breaths, but that is inaccurate. The body and head pillow need to be blow up separately and they take 6 breaths and 2 breaths respectively, equaling a total of 8 breaths to blow it up. I was giving large, full breaths when testing this item out. Now, this is only 3 extra breaths when compared to the manufacturers’ suggested amount, which in reality is only a couple extra seconds. No big deal.

Now, my wife (5’9, 150 pounds), my daughter (5’9, 142 pounds) and I (5’10, 170 pounds) all tried this sleep pack out on tile floor once it was blown up. My wife and I are in our late fifties, our daughter in her mid-twenties, and we all thought it was pretty comfortable. We each laid on our backs and our sides. My wife has back problems and thought the body part was still comfortable, though she did complain about the pillow. My daughter and I both liked the pillow very much because it almost provides a pocket to cradle your head, and it’s awesome whether you are sleeping on your back or side. The bottom of the sleeping back has the holes filled in; my daughter suggested carry this design feature up the spine to provide a little bit more support and comfort, as her tailbone and hips fell in the cracks and were a bit uncomfortable. I didn’t have an issue and thought it was comfortable. Keep in mind we didn’t sleep in this throughout the night, only tested it for about 10-15 minutes each.

Rolling this pack up to its compact state is pretty simple. I wasn’t able to fit it perfectly back in the bag, but with practice I’m sure I could. Overall, I like the pack and think it will be attractive to people looking to go ultra-light. I think you might sacrifice a little comfort in order for it to be compact and lightweight, but choose your battles. If you’re looking for a lightweight, compact option that does provide some decent support, I would recommend this sleeping mat.
text_fidelity_b: Klymit Inertia O Zone Lightweight Camping Air Pad

Valor Fitness These squat stands are exactly what i was looking for. they are versatile enough to use with a bench or as a squat rack. They are very sturdy, although you need to have extra weight plates on the bottom pegs if you're doing really heavy weights.

I'm a 5'2" woman about 115 pounds so I dont have a huge amount of weights on these when I'm doing workouts. I think the most I've had is about 70lbs. But, one of the great features of these stands is that the adjustable height and anchor on the top allow me to also use these for chin ups! yep, I raise these up high enough so that I can put a low step underneath then jump up to a chin up position on the bar. I have my legs bent at the knees and crossed when I lower so I don't hit the floor. for the chin-ups I have about 40lbs of barbells on the bar and at least 30lbs on the bottom pegs of each stand and these are very sturdy.

I haven't actually used them for a bench press yet, just for squats and the chin-ups, but there is a safety bracket, plus a holder for the barbell when you're doing bench press. all of these are adjustable, too. When doing squats, the legs at the bottom have a thinner bar on one side that when you are ready to get the bar off the rack and step back, you don't have to worry about tripping over the bar at the bottom. Smart design. these guys were really thinking when they made these.

I wanted sturdy stands that were adjustable and could be easily moved if I needed more space. I probably could have gone with a slightly cheaper model, given that these are designed for 600lbs but I really like these stands and if one of my sons or my man decide to ever join me in working out, they can easily use these as well.

if you have a home gym and need something that will give you flexibility for space and plenty of options for your strength training, these are for you!

oh, and if you're a woman looking for a good weight program, I highly recommend [[ASIN:1583333398 The New Rules of Lifting for Women: Lift Like a Man, Look Like a Goddess]] - great program! (and don't for one minute think you're going to "bulk up" -- not gonna happen unless you've got tons of testosterone in you).
text_fidelity_b: Valor Fitness

Hem WiFi Spotting Scope Camera I bought an SME Bullseye WiFi Ammocam in 2017. It has the same connection problems as described for this spotting scope camera.

I came here thinking, "Hey, maybe a camera on my spotting scope would work better than that really expensive WiFi target camera I bought that never worked, even after I sent it back, twice."

Then I saw the brand "SME." Same scam, different product. They can't figure how to make their camera connect to the phone. Even from 5 feet, much less 100 yards.

I spent my entire time trying to get the Bullseye AmmoCam to connect, walking back and forth 100 yards to adjust the antenna, etc. It would connect, then disconnect, then connect, then freeze and lock up.

My favorite use of the Bullseye AmmoCam was when I saw a guy accidentally shoot his brand new SME Bullseye AmmoCam with a .223 round, right through the lith-ion battery pack. The entire plastic ammocam smoked, then burned up -- battery, antenna, wiring and camera. Glorious billows of smoke that stunk to high heaven. Fried everything. Don't mess with burning lithium-ion batteries. And don't shoot them!

A perfect ending to a useless product.

iLuv Smashbox Pro 3.5mm Aux Portable Speaker Case with Built in Hands Free Calling for Smartphones (iPhone 6, 5, 4) Ipad-Black I am surprised at how functional this little gadget is. My smartphone fits right into the protective case and the tiny speakers plug into my phone's headset jack. I can play music or talk on the phone.

* One thing that is especially nice for me is that it holds my phone securely in place and zips shut. I like that because I have one of those phones with a slide-out keyboard - making the rubberized protective case an awkward fit, and the protective case that fits my phone will not stay on. I have dropped my phone several times without any protection and I am surprised that it hasn't broken. This case solves that problem, by containing the entire phone zipped in. It is VERY protective and secure.

* Another thing I like is that the speakers (though small) have a surprisingly good sound. I can listen to music or audio books easily, as long as there is no loud noise around to drown out the sound. This is especially pleasing to me because my phone speakers are not really loud enough to hear much and I have a lot of trouble with my bluetooth device. Since the audio is not wireless and plugs directly into the headset jack, it really simplifies my listening experience.

* Additionally, the speaker jack is not confined to a cell phone. My laptop had terrible sound and when I want to give it a boost, I plug this little device into my computer's headset jack and it gives me just the amount of volume I need without having to mess with bulky speakers.

The negatives are:

* This case is larger than some people would like. I don't mind it, but if you like to carry your cell phone in your pocket, you will not be able to do that while the phone is in this case. It fits nicely into a purse, though.

* The audio uses 2 AA batteries and does not interface with your phone battery. The case cannot be recharged or plugged in, but you will need to continually replace batteries. So far, I have had this case for a week and use it constantly. It still has the original two batteries that I put into it. Your phone will need to be recharged separately from the audio case.

* If you use your phone for other functions besides simply listening to music or talking, they you have to take it out of the case. When secured in this case, the phone is not accessible except for the audio and for answering calls. You will not be able to make calls, use navigation, check email, etc, unless you take your phone out of the case. Again, this isn't a problem for me, but a lot of people like to have their phone immediately accessible for all functions.

* While the sound is perfectly adequate for inside a car or indoors, I think it might be a challenge to hear it well outdoors. This is a SMALL case wirh SMALL speakers - think old fashioned transistor radio. This is NOT a boombox! ;-) If I want to listen to music outdoors, I use headphones. This functions well if I am driving, sewing, or doing dishes, etc.

All in all, I am getting a lot of use from this device. I really love it and don't know how I ever got along without it. I can see how it might not serve everyone's needs but it is great for mine.
text_fidelity_b: iLuv Smashbox Pro 3.5mm Aux Portable Speaker Case with Built in Hands Free Calling for Smartphones (iPhone 6, 5, 4) Ipad-Black

text_fidelity_a:

We are well into our second pair of gloves at this point (got them in AUG, now Dec), and they have held up much better. However, the sticky factor is long gone as the material doesn't seem to keep that aspect. I purchased a bottle of GloveGlu which has fixed that issue.

I have increased the review to three stars, had the initial pair of gloves been as good as the second pair this would be a 4 star review. I think it odd, that the "pattern" in these reviews is the first pair of gloves tend to be less than quality, and then the second pair meets expectations. I would suggest that whoever is "making" the gloves need to improve their quality inspection as they gloves do not seem to be meeting the owners expectations, and it can't be good for the bottom line of the company to continue to reissue new gloves and give discounts on the original purchase to make it right. We purchase a new set every year, if the product would have had the quality of the second issue, I would have bought next years set from this company; however, given the pattern of the reviews, that may not be the case.

Once again customer service was 5 star, in the end the review is about the product, customer service should have never been involved nor a second pair of gloves. That combined with the pattern of the reviews, I feel 3 star (for this experience) is justified.

A bit disappointed in the gloves, we bought on May 18th it is now July 24th and they seem to showing signs of wear already the last set of gloves didn't show for 8 months or so. They also do not seem as "sticky" as the previous pair.

With that said my 11 year old plays year round both indoor and out, uses the gloves three times a week for practice plus 1-2 games a weekend. Seems as if he is dropping more balls than he use to as they gloves don't seem to have kept their grip. So now I am stuck with either paying $15 - $30 bucks for some glove stick or applying that amount toward another pair of gloves 2 months after these were purchases.

All in all fairly disappointed in the gloves.

UPDATE: WOW! What Customer Service, within two days of this post, I heard from the owner of the company who believed the gloves could have been defective AND he sent overnight a new pair so my son would have them for his weekend games.

I am certainly eager to see how the new set of gloves wear this go around and really hope they are as good as the customer service. Will Update later.
text_fidelity_b: Renegade GK Talon Goalie Gloves with Microbe-Guard (Sizes 5-11, 5 Styles, Level 3) Pro-Tek Fingersaves & 3.5+3MM Hyper Grip XD | Durable Goalkeeper Glove for All-Around Play | Based in The USA
